newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN envoy heads for Zaire to probe massacre reports.
newsitem.headline: UN envoy heads for Zaire to probe massacre reports.

text.p: A United Nations special human rights investigator has left for Zaire to investigate reports of alleged massacres by mainly Tutsi rebels in the east, a U.N. statement said on Tuesday.
It said the investigator, Roberto Garreton, would spend a week in eastern Zaire to gather evidence on reported abuses.

Garreton says he has received many charges of extremely grave human rights violations in areas taken by mainly Tutsi rebels, who began fighting in October to topple President Mobutu Sese Seko and now control much of the east of the vast country.
He will report his findings to the U.N. Human Rights Commission meeting in Geneva until April 18, the statement said.

Zaire's main human rights group, the Association for the Defence of Human Rights in Zaire (Azadho), has alleged large-scale massacres of Rwandan Hutus by rebels at Mugunga, Kibumba, and Katale camps which the rebels overran last year.
It has cited dates, places, witnesses and grave sites to back charges against the rebels and their alleged Rwandan and Ugandan army backers.

Hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Hutus fled to Zaire and Tanzania after Tutsi-led forces seized power in 1994 to halt genocidal killings of Tutsis and moderate Hutus by Rwanda's former Hutu army and militiamen.
Many of the refugees, who had been used as human shields by Hutu troops fleeing the victorious Tutsis, have returned home.

But more than 300,000 remain unaccounted for in east Zaire, where the world's powers refused to send in troops late last year to separate the refugees from extremist Hutu militiamen, setting the stage for today's conflict.
